units.translation: The commentators [derive it] from (Odyss. 22, 412.) “οὐχ ὁσίη φθιμένοισιν ἐπ᾿ ἀνδράσιν εὐχετάασθαι” [it is not holy to boast over slain men] so that the sense is: but death, the slayer of men, not boasting over the end from the gods on high, will leave the heights of the immortals and come upon the enemies. Eust. p. 437, 20: from ἐναίρειν [to slay] and κτείνειν [to kill] comes ἐναροκτάντας [slaying men], death. From the corrupt words which are read between ἐναροκτάντας δὲ [but the slayer of men] and ὑψοῦ [on high], Hermann restored a tolerable sense: ἐναροκτάντας δὲ φθόνος αὐχαῖς | ἔγκοτος ὑψοῦ | τέλος ἀθανάτων ἀπολείψει, | ἥξει τ᾽ ἐχθρούς [but envy, wrathful at the boasts of the slayer of men, will leave on high the end of the immortals and will come upon the enemies].
But the slayer of men ... wrath on high will leave the end of the immortals (Musurus rightly corrected to ἀπολείψει [will leave]).
